item.title: Ole Miss had FBI agent sweep football facility for bugs after Lane Kiffin left for LSU
item.description: Ole Miss officials feared electronic surveillance after Lane Kiffin took multiple assistants to LSU ahead of the college football playoff game.
item.content:encoded:
Would it be shocking to learn that Ole Miss officials had someone with FBI ties help check its football facility in the days following Lane Kiffin’s departure for LSU?

Sure, if college athletics were operating in anything resembling normal times.

But with former NFL players now finding paths back to college football and Congress debating legislation that could limit coaches from leaving during a season, almost nothing feels too absurd anymore.

NCAA Created This Mess, Now LSU Set To Make Dae’Quan Wright College Football’s First NFL Returnee

Walker Jones, the executive director of Ole Miss’ NIL collective, recently appeared on the "Assorted Crackers" podcast — yes, that is the name — to discuss the madness surrounding Kiffin’s exit for LSU.

During a conversation about coaches who were contractually tied to both Ole Miss and LSU, Jones revealed an unreported detail from the days leading up to the Rebels’ College Football Playoff appearance without Kiffin.

Technically, the FBI was involved.

"We actually had the FBI come through and walk the building for bugs and for everything," Walker Jones told 'Assorted Crackers'". "We knew kind of what was in Baton Rouge, and we knew how they operated. I remember getting on my knees and looking underneath the desk, like checking for, 'Is there some sort of bug in my office?'"

PETE GOLDING DROPS UNFILTERED TRUTH ON 'EX' LANE KIFFIN, AND NCAA TAMPERING: 'WHAT HAVE WE CREATED?'

So, did Ole Miss bring in federal agents to sweep its facility for listening devices, straight out of a Jason Bourne movie?

Well, not exactly. But, yes there was a search.

.

On Monday, while Kiffin was fielding questions in Baton Rouge about LSU adding former NFL players to its roster, the questions in Oxford were a bit different.

What exactly happened with that FBI search of the Ole Miss football facility?

Head coach Pete Golding did not deny that a sweep occurred, though he offered an explanation that made far more sense than the image of agents descending on the Manning Center with bug detectors.

"Any bowl game, playoff system, obviously you're gonna up security," Golding told reporters. I'm not sure there was a hiring process of here we go with the FBI. I do think we probably have a current player whose dad just so happens to work for the FBI and that lives in town. There was no measure to go 'oh my gosh, come in from that standpoint'.

"Obviously any time you get into that playoff system and you got guys going from this building to other places (LSU), you want to make sure it's secure for your players. The video access, everything else you're doing regardless where you're at....No, there was no hiring process of 'let's get the FBI in here, holy cow, they start looking around'. It wasn’t anything like that."

When Kiffin left Ole Miss for LSU, he took multiple assistants with him to Baton Rouge. During the chaotic stretch before Ole Miss played Tulane in the College Football Playoff, some coaches were traveling back and forth between Baton Rouge and Oxford.

Kiffin was also expected to target multiple Ole Miss players once the Rebels’ season ended, including Kewan Lacy and Trinidad Chambliss.

LSU’S LANE KIFFIN FIRES BACK AT NFL RETURNEE BACKLASH: BLAME THE NCAA, NOT US FOR RECRUITING PRO ATHLETES

Add in the growing paranoia across college athletics about practice footage and other team materials being illegally accessed through video databases, and it is not hard to understand why Ole Miss took extra precautions.

One of the most chaotic times in recent college athletics memory will one day turn into a movie that will have the feel of a spy-thriller directed by Michael Bay.

Just days before the season begins, coaches are explaining why former NFL players belong back on college rosters. The NCAA is spending what feels like every day in a courtroom. Congress is still being asked to fix a system that has become nearly impossible to govern.

And on Sept. 19, 2025, Ole Miss and LSU will meet in Oxford in a game that already feels destined to become one of the most entertaining weekends of the season.

PETE GOLDING MAKES IT KNOWN HE HAS TAMPERING RECEIPTS, WHILE ALSO ADMITTING KIFFIN TEXTS HIM WAY TOO MUCH

Between talk of "basket-weaving" classes at Ole Miss, Kiffin’s recruiting comments, eligibility lawsuits, Texas Tech’s Brendan Sorsby saga and endless congressional debates, college football needs actual games back in a hurry.

Still, who doesn’t enjoy a good FBI story in college athletics?

Well, perhaps Will Wade — or the folks at Michigan.

item.title: Putin ‘panicked’ as defiant Ukraine marks Independence Day under Russian bombardment
item.description: Ukraine celebrated 35 years of independence amid fresh Russian attacks as an expert said Kyiv’s deep strikes and battlefield pressure have left Putin rattled.
item.content:encoded:
Ukraine marked its 35th Independence Day on Monday under the shadow of continued Russian attacks, with one regional security expert arguing that Russian President Vladimir Putin is "panicked" as Ukrainian forces strike deeper inside Russia.

The anniversary, commemorating Ukraine's Aug. 24, 1991, declaration of independence from the Soviet Union, came amid intensified Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure and heightened security concerns after Ukraine's Security Service warned of possible terrorist attacks ahead of the holiday.

European leaders joined Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv for Independence Day events in a show of support as the war grinds on. Zelenskyy declared that Ukraine wants peace but is not prepared to surrender to Moscow's demands.

A Russian drone strike Friday on a packed shopping center in Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskyy’s hometown, killed at least 16 people and injured 130, according to The Associated Press.

'PURE HELL' IN MOSCOW AS UKRAINIAN DRONES STRIKE MAJOR REFINERY SUPPLYING CAPITAL'S FUEL MARKET

Putin has warned that Ukrainian strikes on Russian economic targets open a "Pandora’s box," while Kyiv maintains deep strikes are vital to disrupting Moscow’s logistics.

Ukraine has targeted Russian economic infrastructure, including warehouses belonging to online retailers Wildberries and Ozon.

"The war with Russia has seen a lot of advances for the Ukrainians over this year," former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Carrie Filipetti, now executive director of the Vandenberg Coalition, told Fox News Digital.

"They've recently been able to actually penetrate much deeper into Russian territory, including close to Moscow and St. Petersburg."

"Their success on the military front has now resulted in the Russians getting panicked and starting to attack more inside Ukraine and what they're really trying to do is weaken their will and capabilities," Filipetti said, adding that Putin "gets very anxious when he's put in a corner."

"What we're seeing is these sorts of gasps at trying to retain some kind of control," Filipetti added. "This is why he recently targeted a shopping mall inside Ukrainian territory. He is not focused on targeting military assets. He is really focused on trying to defeat the will of Ukrainians by attacking them."

RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY

Filipetti warned the targeting of civilian areas created heightened security risks as Ukraine marked its 35th Independence Day, more than four years into Russia's full-scale invasion.

Several European leaders traveled to Kyiv for Ukraine’s Independence Day events, including European Council President António Costa and leaders from Finland, Lithuania, Norway, Denmark, Estonia and Latvia.

Filipetti said the high-level participation underscored continued international support for Ukraine.

TRUMP'S TURKEY ARMS SALE PROPOSAL SPARKS CONGRESSIONAL QUESTIONS BEFORE NATO SUMMIT

"Independence Day is a really important moment for the allies of the Ukrainians to really show that we are not losing steam, that we continue to support their operations, to continue to support their sovereignty," Filipetti said. "But anytime there's massive public gatherings, particularly to demonstrate patriotism and support for the Ukrainian state, it increases the security risk."

Ukrainian authorities urged citizens to stay vigilant on public transport and guard against potential sabotage or sharing media that could reveal military positions, as well as possible attacks, Ukrainian News reported.

"They should be particularly mindful about sharing any videos or photographs that could betray the locations of some of their frontline soldiers," Filipetti warned.

DRONE OFFENSIVE HITS RUSSIAN OIL TANKERS AND REFINERIES AT 'INDUSTRIAL SCALE' AS MOSCOW BANS DIESEL EXPORTS

Monday's holiday came after a lethal exchange of drone and missile strikes. Ukrainian officials reported at least seven deaths from Russian attacks, while a Ukrainian drone strike in Russia's Krasnodar region killed three, according to Russian officials, The Associated Press reported.

"The Russians really want to bleed the Ukrainians of people, equipment, and will before the Russians are bled of those same three things," Filipetti said. "And what we've seen over the course of this year is almost no territorial gains on behalf of the Russians."

They are losing more soldiers each month than they can recruit, forcing them to rely on North Korean, Cuban and other foreign fighters to fill the gap, Filipetti added.

ZELENSKYY SAYS PUTIN 'LOST THE INITIATIVE' AS UKRAINE'S TECH INDUSTRY RESHAPES THE WAR

"Remember, Putin thought that this was going to be a special military operation that was going to last a matter of weeks," Filipetti said.

Ultimately, she emphasized that Ukraine's resolve delivers a firm deterrent beyond Moscow.

"It sends a message to the Russians that any invasion of sovereign territory, like their invasion of Ukraine, is going to create more consequences for them," Filipetti said. "We are not losing steam, and we continue to support their operations, to continue to support their sovereignty."

Filipetti said it also sends an important message to other American adversaries like China.

"These adversaries of the United States really learned from how the United States handles conflicts in other theaters. It's really important that our adversaries of China, Russia, Iran, and others understand that if they invade another country unilaterally, there are going to be consequences, not rewards."

item.title: 'National Treasure' director predicts upcoming third film won't be able to 'ignore' politics
item.description: Director Jon Turteltaub said political polarization delayed "National Treasure 3" and explained the finished script will have to address modern politics.
item.content:encoded:
"National Treasure" director Jon Turteltaub suggested Friday that politics was a factor in delaying the third film in the Nicolas Cage-led franchise and predicted the issue would be addressed in the new sequel.

During a live recording of the "National Treasure Hunt" podcast in Philadelphia, Turteltaub confirmed to an audience that "National Treasure 3" was "finally real" with a finished script approved by him and Disney.

The original film, "National Treasure," came out in 2004 with its sequel, "National Treasure: Book of Secrets," premiering three years later in 2007. Both were directed by Turteltaub.

16 PATRIOTIC MOVIES TO WATCH THIS FOURTH OF JULY, FROM 'TOP GUN' TO 'SAVING PRIVATE RYAN'

While discussing the gap between the second and third films, Turteltaub said that the growing political climate in the country made it difficult to keep working on the historical fiction film series, citing an interaction with former Republican House Speaker Kevin McCarthy.

"He, like others, were surprised that Democrats made that movie because Democrats can’t be patriots," Turteltaub said, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer. "That’s the thought and it just got worse. And on the Democrats’ side: ‘Oh, Republicans, they just want to keep stuff to themselves, they hate everybody, they want to kill everyone, and blah blah blah.'"

Though he did not offer many details about the third film, Turteltaub predicted that it would inevitably have to address modern politics.

"We have to be very careful, but I don’t feel we are allowed to ignore it," Turteltaub said. "I think we have to include that idea in the story somehow without making someone feel put off."

KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS IT'S 'EXHAUSTING' WHEN MOVIES TRY TO ALTER HISTORY TO FIT MODERN TASTES

Fox News Digital reached out to Disney for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

Turteltaub and producer Jerry Bruckheimer have hinted at the production of a third film starring Cage for years, though production has yet to take place. Even on the podcast, Turteltaub joked "things could happen" in the meantime.

"Now, it’s Hollywood real, meaning things could happen. Nic gets hit by a bus, there’s no 'National Treasure 3.' If I get hit by a bus, there’s probably a 'National Treasure 3.' Welcome to Hollywood," Turteltaub said.

In a comment to Fox News Digital, film critic Christian Toto, the founder and editor of Hollywood in Toto, said that it made sense for Hollywood to tackle another older franchise for nostalgia but expressed disappointment in the idea of addressing politics.

DISNEY'S POLITICAL FIGHT WITH RON DESANTIS COST COMPANY YEARS OF THEME PARK EXPANSION, COURT RECORDS REVEAL

"It sounds like Turteltaub, a veteran Hollywood director who isn't known for his political views, was accurately assessing how Hollywood views patriotism and the political divide," Toto said. "It's actually a sad sign of the times — a franchise about U.S. history is now seen as problematic or challenging, when it should be nothing of the kind."

"A franchise like this would be best served staying apolitical, and the director's comments suggest a way to thread the needle between acknowledging our political chasm and moving forward with a fresh new story," he added. "Heck, if that delicate balance works, it might be the biggest film in the franchise."

item.title: Kacey Musgraves divides fans with immigrant children’s plea, faces boycott calls to ‘shut up and sing’
item.description: Kacey Musgraves asked fans to donate to the Young Center for Immigrant Children's Rights during her tour opener, sparking a divided reaction on social media.
item.content:encoded:
Kacey Musgraves is facing backlash after asking fans to donate to an immigrant children’s rights group as her birthday wish while kicking off her "Middle of Nowhere" tour.

On Friday, the country music star marked her 38th birthday on the opening night of her tour at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois. At one point, Musgraves paused her show and urged concertgoers to contribute to the Young Center for Immigrant Children's Rights.

"It’s a wonderful organization, and they help give aid — legal aid — and money to children whose parents have been deported unfairly," Musgraves said. "It’s not a political thing. It’s just, these kids need help."

She continued, "They have no guidance and no way to get through this thing without their homebase or their parents. So anyway, 50 cents, whatever the hell, I don't know, whatever you want to do but that would mean a lot to me."

KACEY MUSGRAVES FACES BOYCOTT CALLS AFTER ASKING FANS TO DONATE TO IMMIGRANT CHILDREN'S GROUP

"If you don't want to, that's totally fine too," Musgraves added.

The eight-time Grammy Award winner's appeal was immediately met with applause and cheers from the crowd in Chicago. However, Musgraves' request drew a divided response online, including criticism from conservative political commentators.

"What is an unfair deportation?" Tomi Lahren, host of Outkick's "Tomi Lahren Is Fearless" podcast, wrote on X alongside a video of Musgraves' birthday request.

KENNY CHESNEY TELLS BILL MAHER THE KEY REASON HE REFUSES TO TELL HIS LISTENERS HOW TO VOTE

"Kacey Musgraves stopped her concert to ask the audience to donate money for legal aid to kids whose parents have been deported ‘unfairly.’ How about donating money the help kids who's parents have been killed by illegal immigrants! What happened to the country music industry?" conservative influencer Vince Langman commented.

"Another TRAITOROUS woman who wants nothing more than to see our country fall," an X user chimed in.

"Shut up and sing Kasey (sic)!! Why do musicians think they Can draw a line in the sand? You alienate 50% of your audience," another commented.

Some critics declared that they would no longer support Musgraves and called for a boycott of her music and concerts.

NATALIE MAINES’ ANTI-TRUMP TIRADE, ZACH BRYAN’S FENCE-CLIMBING CLASH FUEL COUNTRY MUSIC’S BIGGEST FEUDS

"You just earned yourself a big ol’ boycott, you traitor," one detractor wrote. "Illegal aliens and their kids don’t deserve our patronage and neither do you!"

"I’m deporting Musgraves from all my music playlists," another X user commented.

Other social media users argued that Musgraves should donate her own money rather than ask fans to contribute.

"Kacey Musgraves is worth $15 million. Yet she’s asking fans who already paid $150 to $350 for tickets to donate to support the children of illegal aliens," one social media user commented. "If she cares that much, she can fund it herself and let them live in one of her multi-million-dollar mansions."

MUSICIAN KENNY CHESNEY'S REFUSAL TO SPEAK OUT ON POLITICS SPARKS ARGUMENT ON 'THE VIEW'

"Everyone she is speaking too (sic) gave her their money when they bought tickets," another added. "She did not give the audience money. So now she has the money, shouldn't she donate to whatever cause she wants? She is actually on stage at a show that the audience had to pay to get admission to and now she is asking for more of their money. That's rude."

However, some of the "Dry Spell" singer's fans defended her on social media and praised her for speaking out on behalf of immigrant children.

POP STAR OLIVIA RODRIGO FELT 'ENRAGED' AFTER ICE USED HER HIT SONG, BRANDS AGENCY 'BARBARIC'

"Love this. 'It's not a political thing. It's just, these kids need help.' Exactly. More artists doing this please," one fan wrote on X.

"In all fairness, the kids didn’t do anything wrong," another wrote. "I don’t believe their parents were wrongfully deported, but I equally believe that their children, if retained in the United States by law, should be taken care of. We’re not f------ animals!"

"No boycott here!" an X user declared.

"Helping children caught in difficult circumstances is a worthy cause," one commenter argued. "At the same time, immigration enforcement and whether a deportation was lawful or justified are matters for the courts and policymakers not concert stages."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Musgraves' representatives for comment.

Meanwhile, Musgraves stood by her remarks on social media, taking to her Instagram Story to upload a post that read, "Kinda chic when kids don't face immigration court alone."

The singer also reposted a message shared by the Young Center's Instagram page, in which the organization expressed its gratitude to her.

"Thank you," the nonprofit wrote. "We appreciate your support of our work and mission to see unaccompanied immigrant children safe, free, and with their families."

Based in Chicago, the Young Center describes its work as pairing volunteers with attorneys and social workers to advocate for unaccompanied and separated immigrant children in government custody. Its website lists family unity, release from custody, fair proceedings and children's best interests among its priorities.

The nonprofit reported serving 1,975 children from 53 countries in 2024 and opening 1,388 new cases. Its 2025 annual report said children's average detention time increased from 30 to 198 days and requests for assistance from detained parents quadrupled from 2024.

Friday’s appeal extended Musgraves’ support for the charity. In April, resale platform Depop announced that 20 pieces from her wardrobe, including clothing from music videos and tours, would be sold in capsule drops. Women's Wear Daily reported that all proceeds would benefit the Young Center.

In announcing the sale, Musgraves described the beneficiary without discussing immigration enforcement.

"I also adore the fact that the sales are supporting a really beautiful cause," Musgraves said.

Musgraves also invited three brothers, ages 18, 14 and 12, to open three Texas shows in May after their family was released from ICE custody. The mariachi performers' family said they entered through the now-defunct CBP One appointment system in 2023 and sought asylum after fleeing violence in Mexico, KSAT reported.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

DHS said the family entered illegally and had been released into the country by the Biden administration. Responding to the family’s detention, DHS said federal law required custody while its immigration claims were heard.

"The law requires illegal aliens who show up at a port of entry without valid entry to be detained while all their claims are heard. You can look it up in the statute," a DHS spokesperson told KSAT. "Unlike the previous administration, the Trump administration is not going to ignore the rule of law."

Musgraves' latest remarks came as ICE enforcement reached record levels. Federal sources told Fox News Digital that agents made about 51,000 immigration arrests in July, topping the previous record of roughly 43,000 in June.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Every day, the brave men and women of ICE are arresting and DEPORTING dangerous criminal illegal aliens, including gang members, from our country," DHS said.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

The Chicago concert launched Musgraves’ North American arena tour, with Midland as the opening act. Official tour listings showed dates continuing through October.

Fox News Digital's CJ Womack contributed to this report.

item.title: NFL Sunday Ticket is no longer worth the price | Bobby Burack
item.description: NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube costs up to $480, but expanded primetime windows on Netflix and Amazon Prime mean fewer out-of-market games remain.
item.content:encoded:
You may have received an email over the past week about renewing or adding NFL Sunday Ticket, YouTube's exclusive package for out-of-market NFL games.

You may also have noticed the price. It is expensive. And each year, the NFL further reduces the package's value by expanding its national windows.

Let us explain.

Sunday Ticket does not include nationally televised games or games available in your local market. Subscribers do not receive Thursday Night Football, Sunday Night Football, or Monday Night Football. Nor does the package include the three or four games available locally across Fox and CBS during the 1 p.m. and 4:25 p.m. ET windows.

For example, viewers in Michigan cannot watch Lions games on Sunday Ticket because those games air locally on Fox or CBS.

We agree. The NFL's television schedule is unnecessarily complicated. And it's getting worse.

RESTAURANT ASSOCIATIONS URGE CONGRESS TO ACT AS NFL SUNDAY TICKET STREAMING SWITCH THREATENS BAR REVENUES

Netflix will carry five games this season: 49ers-Rams from Australia in Week 1 on Thursday night, the first Thanksgiving Eve matchup between the Packers and Rams, two Christmas Day games, and an unannounced Saturday game later in the season.

Yes, Thanksgiving Eve means the NFL will play on a Wednesday. And because Netflix will air a Thursday night game in Week 1, NBC will move its Patriots-Seahawks season opener also to a Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026.

The NFL will then play four Friday games: Packers-Bears and Bills-Broncos on Netflix, Rams-Seahawks on Fox on Christmas Day, and Broncos-Steelers on Amazon Prime on Black Friday.

In total, the NFL will play six games on Wednesdays and Fridays this season, two days it long avoided (in part because of legal restrictions).

Further, nine of the league's 18 weeks will include an international game, most of which will air on NFL Network at 9:30 a.m. ET.

WATCHING THE NFL WILL COST MORE, REQUIRE MORE STREAMING SERVICES THAN EVER THIS SEASON

What does this have to do with Sunday Ticket?

Each time the NFL sells a new national window to a broadcaster, it removes a game that otherwise would have been part of the Sunday early or late-afternoon slate.

The result is fewer games on Sunday Ticket, but for a higher price.

YouTube lists the standard price for 2026-27 Sunday Ticket at $480. Subscribers can divide the cost into eight $60 monthly payments, but they must eventually pay in full. You cannot subscribe and unsubscribe by the month.

Most users can purchase it for less. The $480 price is misleading. It largely exists so the NFL can market lower prices as discounts.

New users can currently sign up for $240 a year. Most returning subscribers can renew for $336. YouTube TV subscribers can purchase the package for $234, though they must maintain their YouTube TV subscription throughout the NFL season.

Teachers, military members, veterans, first responders and medical workers can purchase Sunday Ticket for $198 per year through ID.me. Eligible students can get it for $119, though they can stream on only one device.

The price varies by subscriber. Still, Sunday Ticket lasts just four months. At any of those prices, it remains one of the most expensive streaming subscriptions available.

And because of the scheduling changes cited above, the number of games no longer justifies the cost. Again, most of the week's best matchups will air elsewhere.

'NFL REDZONE' HOST SCOTT HANSON SAYS HE UNDERSTANDS FAN FRUSTRATION OVER COSTLY STREAMING SUBSCRIPTIONS

At this point, Sunday Ticket might be most appealing for fans who live outside the market of their favorite team.

Then again, it may still depend on the team for which you root.

The following teams have have no traditional primetime games scheduled this season (this could change with late-season flexing): Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans, Miami Dolphins, and Las Vegas Raiders have no traditional primetime games scheduled this season.

Sunday Ticket is the only way for fans of those teams to watch them weekly from a a different state.

By contrast, the Los Angeles Rams, Kansas City Chiefs, Buffalo Bills, Seattle Seahawks, Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers each have at least six primetime games. In addition, Fox and CBS will likely feature them heavily in the 1 p.m. and 4:25 p.m. windows available to most of the country (so long as the local team is not airing at the same time on the same channel).

In sum, a Chiefs fan in North Carolina likely won't need Sunday Ticket to watch their team most weeks, a Titans fan in Arizona will.

The NFL got greedy. Sunday Ticket's diminished value is a consequence. And as the league continues to expand its national windows, demand for the package will decline.

Unless, of course, the NFL lowers the price.

item.title: North Carolina doctor accused of shooting 2 sisters in alleged interstate road rage attack
item.description: North Carolina doctor Richard Thomas Arriviello allegedly shot two sisters in a Jeep on Interstate 77 during a road rage incident before fleeing.
item.content:encoded:
A North Carolina doctor was arrested Aug. 22 after he allegedly fired into a Jeep during an interstate road rage incident, wounding two sisters, ages 12 and 20, according to Virginia State Police.

Dr. Richard Thomas Arriviello, 61, of Charlotte, North Carolina, was driving north on Interstate 77 in his Mercedes-Benz around 8:50 a.m. when gunfire erupted about three miles north of the North Carolina-Virginia state line.

State police said in a press release that Arriviello fired into the moving Jeep, striking both sisters in the legs.

Both victims were airlifted to a hospital with injuries that were not considered life-threatening, according to police.

'TESLA ROAD RAGE DRIVER' SENTENCED TO SEVEN YEARS IN PRISON AFTER ATTACKING MOTHER AND DAUGHTER IN HAWAII

Arriviello then fled in his Mercedes-Benz, police said.

Troopers spotted and stopped the Mercedes-Benz about 15 miles away and took Arriviello into custody.

Arriviello faces several felony charges, including malicious shooting into an occupied vehicle, maliciously causing bodily harm to another with intent to maim and use of a firearm while committing a felony.

Arriviello remains jailed without bond at the New River Valley Regional Jail, officials told Fox News Digital. He is scheduled to appear in court Sept. 29.

State police have not said what led to the alleged road rage encounter or whether investigators recovered a firearm from Arriviello’s Mercedes-Benz.

The Jeep’s driver was also cited for reckless driving, but authorities did not identify the driver.

SEE IT: DASHCAM SHOWS FLORIDA TROOPER CHASING ALLEGED STREET TAKEOVER SUSPECT AT 140 MPH

North Carolina Medical Board records show Arriviello has been licensed as an emergency medicine physician in the state since 2010 and has no public disciplinary actions listed against him.

The records list Arriviello as the owner of Family Urgent Care in Monroe.

Fox News Digital reached out to Family Urgent Care in Monroe and Virginia State Police for additional comment.

item.title: ‘Moderate’ Dem gubernatorial candidate embraced DEI budget tool, Green New Deal-style policies
item.description: Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley emerged as the more moderate alternative to democratic socialist Francesca Hong, but his record includes racial-equity budgeting, net-zero climate goals and more.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic socialist Francesca Hong lost Wisconsin’s Democratic gubernatorial primary earlier this month, but some of the progressive policies that define the party’s far-left flank may not have disappeared with her campaign entirely.

David Crowley, the Milwaukee County executive who defeated Hong after being cast as the more moderate choice, has overseen racial-equity budgeting, expanded the county’s equity bureaucracy and urged the Wisconsin attorney general to sue fossil fuel companies for environmental-related damages. Meanwhile, Crowley has also shared ground with Hong on taxing millionaires and ambitious carbon-neutrality goals.

"Milwaukee County is known for it's beer and brats, but unfortunately it's also the epicenter of David Crowley's budgetary boondoggles. Under Crowley's failed leadership, residents received their largest property tax hike in 15 years, paid higher sales taxes for everyday purchases, and saw millions of their hard-earned tax dollars set up to finance Crowley's Green New Deal 'Net Zero' scam for the county," Wisconsin native and Republican consultant Mark Bednar told Fox News Digital. 

"In an era where voters are increasingly focused on the economy and their pocketbooks, Wisconsinites should ask themselves, do they really want to expand Crowley's gross mismanagement and liberal priorities to the whole state?" He continued. "I'm guessing a big Wisconsin 'heck no.'"

WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC VOTERS CHALK SOCIALIST FRANCESCA HONG'S STUNNING LOSS UP TO ELECTABILITY CONCERNS

In a recent campaign ad, Crowley touted a record of "getting things done" and "practical bipartisan solutions," while Wisconsin Public Radio described him during the primary as a "mainstream Democratic alternative" to Hong. 

CBS News called him a "moderate Democrat" after his primary victory, while Axios framed Crowley's upset as a potential revival for the Democratic Party’s center-left.

But, despite being cast as the more moderate alternative, Crowley has shared several significant policy positions with Hong. Crowley himself acknowledged the policy overlap during the primary, telling supporters that "there’s many things that everybody agrees on, right?" when discussing his differences with Hong, according to WISN 12’s "UpFront," while adding that there were also areas where the two "absolutely disagree."

Both have backed higher taxes on millionaires, a $20 minimum wage, expanded union rights and universal child care. Their climate agendas also contain a notable parallel – Hong campaigned on making Wisconsin carbon-neutral by 2050, while Crowley signed Milwaukee County’s plan to bring county operations to net-zero emissions by the same year.

AOC BLASTED AS TOO MODERATE BY MAOIST DSA FACTION AS 2028 BUZZ GROWS

Crowley’s record on DEI complicates his "moderate" image as well. It includes embedding a Racial Equity Budget Tool (REBT) into the state budgeting process. Milwaukee County describes the tool as a "structured racial equity lens" for departments to assess how budget decisions affect communities of color. 

In his 2022 budget address, Crowley said all the Milwaukee County departments had "once again" used the tool and were asked what they would do with additional funding "to specifically address racial equity."

"Racism is a public health crisis in Milwaukee County," the county's 2024 budget stated. "The REBT is a structured racial equity lens for Milwaukee County departments to use to critically assess the impact of budget decisions on communities of color."

Crowley’s tenure as Milwaukee County executive also transformed the county’s Office on African American Affairs into a broader "Office of Equity," which grew the original office’s reach to "other communities of color, LGBTQ+ and people with varying abilities," while increasing accountability for the county’s existing racial-equity goals.

Climate policy has been another focus of Crowley’s tenure in Milwaukee. In April 2025, he signed Milwaukee County’s Climate Action 2050 plan, developed by his administration after the County Board adopted a carbon-neutrality goal in 2021. The plan seeks to bring county government operations to net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 — the same year Hong’s statewide climate agenda called for Wisconsin to become carbon-neutral.

Crowley also signed a 2022 resolution calling on Wisconsin’s attorney general to sue fossil-fuel companies and seek damages for environmental and climate harm in Wisconsin communities. And, in April, he signed legislation reaffirming Milwaukee County’s commitment to the principles and goals of the Paris Agreement amid federal climate-policy rollbacks.

Crowley’s campaign and Milwaukee County’s press office did not respond to Fox News Digital’s requests for comment on his record.

item.title: Rare signed Picasso print stolen from gallery turns up in vacant apartment years later
item.description: Pablo Picasso's signed "Torero" etching, appraised at up to $50,000, resurfaced after a Milwaukee landlord spotted it hanging in an evicted apartment.
item.content:encoded:
A signed Pablo Picasso etching stolen from a Wisconsin art gallery nearly a decade ago has been recovered after a Milwaukee landlord turned the artwork in to police, authorities said.

The original 1949 Picasso etching, titled "Torero," was brought into Milwaukee Police Department (MPD) District Four on Aug. 5, after the person who found it suspected it had been stolen, the MPD said.

An authenticator confirmed the next day that it was the same print reported stolen from a Milwaukee art gallery in the 700 block of North Jefferson Street on Feb. 16, 2018, police said.

FBI TRACKS DOWN CENTURIES-OLD CHRISTIAN ARTIFACT IN UNEXPECTED PLACE: 'INCREDIBLY EXCITING'

"The Milwaukee Police Department is grateful that this community member recognized the etching print and did the right thing and returned it," the MPD said.

Milwaukee landlord Tim Dertz found the rare print by the renowned Spanish sculptor and painter while cleaning out a Bay View apartment after an eviction, WISN-TV reported.

Picasso died in 1973 at age 91.

"It was kind of in a weird spot hanging on a wall," Dertz told the news station. He said the artwork appeared to have been there for a long time because it had collected "tons of dust" across the top.

WILT CHAMBERLAIN WARM-UP JACKET BOUGHT FOR $3 AT THRIFT STORE SELLS FOR TENS OF THOUSANDS

Dertz showed the print to an antique dealer friend, who recognized it as a Picasso and said he believed it could be the artwork stolen from Bill DeLind’s Milwaukee gallery years earlier, The Associated Press reported.

Dertz then turned the print over to police, who contacted DeLind to examine it.

HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS IN STOLEN GOODS RECOVERED AT A USED CAR LOT AFTER ADULT TOY COMPANY PURCHASE

DeLind told the AP he immediately recognized the stolen "Torero," which is one of 30 known copies signed by Picasso. His DeLind Fine Art Appraisals sticker was still attached to the back of the framed artwork.

"I was overwhelmed," DeLind said. "It was indeed mine. It came back full circle."

TITANIC SURVIVOR'S LIFE JACKET SELLS FOR OVER $900K AT AUCTION, FAR EXCEEDING PRICE EXPECTATIONS

The print was appraised at between $35,000 and $50,000 when it was stolen, DeLind told the AP. He said its value may now be closer to $50,000 given the story behind its recovery.

The artwork remains in Milwaukee police custody while the client who commissioned it for sale through DeLind’s gallery works through insurance matters, according to the AP.

Milwaukee police told WISN the statute of limitations for theft and property crimes is generally six years, though the investigation remains open.

DeLind said his former business partner, who died in February, was devastated by the 2018 theft and called police every year on the anniversary of the crime to urge renewed publicity in hopes of finding the piece.

"He would have been over the moon about this," DeLind told the AP.

Milwaukee police told Fox News Digital that no additional information is available beyond what the department has already released.

item.title: Five best hikes in Tallahassee to try ahead of Florida State and New Mexico State's Week Zero showdown
item.description: Five Tallahassee hiking trails offer college football travelers stunning north Florida scenery ahead of the Florida State Week Zero showdown.
item.content:encoded:
College football is officially here, and that means traveling to different parts of the country to see the games this season.

The beauty of college football is that most of the games don't take place in some overcrowded metropolitan area, so you'll be able to take in all the natural wonders of a particular venue.

Here at OutKick OutDoors, we wanted to provide you lovers of nature with some of the best hiking spots to hit each week you decide to make the trek to a different college town, and first up on the docket is Tallahassee for the Week Zero showdown between New Mexico State and Florida State.

FOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL FANS, "NO FALL WEDDINGS" ISN'T A BIT OR A GIMMICK, IT'S A LIFESTYLE

Before we begin, a quick reminder that although college football normally means fall weather and mild temperatures, this is still the Florida panhandle in August, so most hikes will happen under some extreme heat conditions.

Dress and pack accordingly and make sure you are staying hydrated.

Believe me, there's no humidity like Florida humidity, and if you aren't careful, you'll end up in the ER on game day surrounded by college kids who went hard in a different direction.

With that out of the way, here are some of the best hikes Tally has to offer.

If you want the best overall hike in the Tallahassee area, this is the move.

Lake Overstreet has about five miles of multi-use trails through live oaks (a northern Florida staple), hills and ravines surrounding a secluded 144-acre lake.

The whole area looks a lot like southern Georgia with its hilly terrain, which can be a nice departure from the typically flat walks that the Sunshine State offers.

THE BEST OUTDOOR WEEKEND IN NORTHWEST GEORGIA DOESN’T REQUIRE 'ROUGHING IT' OR SLEEPING ON THE GROUND

Situated a few miles from downtown Tallahassee, Lake Overstreet offers a serene experience to take your mind off the stresses of a game week, and if you're so inclined, the nearby Lake Hall has kayak rentals available to add a little water action to your hike.

Anyone traveling to Tallahassee from out-of-state needs to make the Miccosukee Canopy Road Greenway a must-see on their itinerary.

The scenery is so quintessential North Florida, with the giant oaks forming the canopy overhead that gives the trail its namesake and the rolling countryside is very evocative of the Deep South.

This is also a nice, relaxing walk for anyone not looking to overdo it while they are in town, as it's less strenuous than some of the more advanced surrounding trails.

If you're looking for something that screams rural Tally, give this one a try.

For those hikers feeling more adventurous, Lafayette Heritage Trail Park offers a bit more trail time than the previous two on the list.

The woods and trail network make this a natural choice for both hikers and mountain bikers, though that phraseology feels a little silly in a flat state like Florida.

Nevertheless, bikers will find plenty to like about Lafayette Heritage Trail Park, and the views of the lake at sunrise and sunset are picturesque.

A special mention needs to be made for the wooden pedestrian bridge to the north of the lake that goes over the railroad tracks.

It looks like something straight out of Adventureland at Disney World and makes for a great photo op.

Perhaps the most "wild" of all the trails listed here, the Munson Hills Off-Road Bike Trailhead offers a more rugged approach to Tallahassee for those seeking more of a challenge.

A pine-forest landscape nestled against the Apalachicola National Forest region, this trail will give a stiff test to all but the most seasoned flatland hikers.

Munson Hills represents the less-manicured option for those who are looking for a trail that's more in tune with nature, but be sure to pack plenty of snacks and water, because this one is a doozy.

It's a little off the beaten path, sitting just south of the Tallahassee city limits, but that's just what we want from our nature hikes!

Call it burying the lead if you want, but I saved the best trail for last.

Lake Jackson Mounds State Park is an absolute treasure, featuring the preserves of ancient Indigenous ceremonial mounds as well as a 0.75-mile interpretive trail past the site of an early-1800s grist mill plus a 2.2-mile nature trail.

It's basically a hike through hundreds of years of Tallahassee history.

A fair warning, though: according to the park's website, the boardwalk to the large mound remains closed.

Everything else here is fair game, and it's all set to the backdrop of North Florida foliage, giving hikers the perfect taste of Tallahassee for their game week trip.

item.title: Democrat rips Hasan Piker as 'hack who thrives on hate' over his warning to American Jews about Israel
item.description: Rep. Hillary Scholten condemned Hasan Piker's remarks about American Jews and Israel, calling the Twitch streamer a "hack who thrives on hate."
item.content:encoded:
Controversial far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who has become increasingly prominent in Democratic politics, is facing backlash from Rep. Hillary Scholten, D-Mich., over his remarks about American Jews' support for Israel that she characterized as "talk of violence" targeting Jewish Michigan state Sen. Jeremy Moss.

In a statement published Monday, Scholten said Piker was "a hack who thrives on hate, shock and awe because he lacks substance."

"Hasan Piker's talk of violence against American Jews, and directly naming a Michigan elected official, and future member of Congress, Jeremy Moss, is unacceptable. Full stop," Scholten's statement read. "We should all be calling out this disgusting rhetoric so it loses its grip on our politics once and for all. It has no place in Michigan, and no place in our country."

HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS

In his response to Scholten's statement, Piker called Scholten an "Israel 1st congresswoman."

"if i was an israel 1st congresswoman with a possible cheating scandal with a republican in the state, i wouldn’t spend so much time vying for the spotlight by actively defaming a prominent antizionist voice to harm the dem senate majority chances over a 90/10 issue," Piker wrote on X.

Piker, who holds a large social media following, has been particularly visible in Michigan this election cycle. He backed Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, who defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in a primary earlier this month. El-Sayed was criticized for appearing with Piker during his campaign, with some saying that the streamer's rhetoric was too extreme.

Scholten backed Stevens last month, calling her a "smart, capable, and common-sense leader." She later praised Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer for endorsing Stevens.

El-Sayed also responded to Piker's comments, and while he did not condemn the streamer outright, he denounced antisemitism and rhetoric that puts the Jewish community in danger.

"I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past," El-Sayed wrote.

"My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters," he added. "Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk."

EL-SAYED DISAVOWS HASAN PIKER'S 9/11 COMMENTS BUT DECRIES 'CANCEL CULTURE'

In his statement, El-Sayed stressed that Piker did not speak for his campaign, writing that, "nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople."

In addition to politicians, Piker was also criticized by Jewish organizations. 

In a statement to Fox News Digital, the Jewish Federation of Detroit said that "Hasan Piker’s talk of violence against Jewish Americans while displaying a picture of a Michigan lawmaker who is Jewish is repugnant and antisemitic."

"We call on all responsible leaders to condemn this extremist, attention-seeking conduct which divides Americans, foments hate, and makes our Jewish community less safe," the Jewish Federation of Detroit's statement read.

The American Jewish Committee (AJC) also said on Monday that by using an image of Moss, "Piker put a target on the backs of Sen. Moss, Jewish candidates and officeholders, and American Jews alike."

"Blaming Jews for the antisemitism directed at them is itself antisemitism," AJC wrote on X. "Every public official who has shared his platform now has a choice: denounce this and walk away, or be complicit. There is no third option."

During his Aug. 20 stream, Piker seemed to warn American Jews against supporting Israel, saying that doing so could lead to violence against them.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said.

When he made the comment, Piker had an image of Moss, who is running to fill Stevens' seat, in his background.

Piker's remarks came amid a controversy over an audio clip circulating online in which Moss purportedly said that the "entire purpose" of his congressional campaign was to ensure America's continued support for Israel.

However, the Michigan Democrat said that the clip was fabricated, calling it "a manipulated and unsourced audio, with things I never did and never would say."

"We are in a dangerous era of disinformation. Circulating a lie because it affirms your bias or belief is equally bad whether it comes from the left or the right. We all have a choice not to spread fabricated images, videos, and audio about candidates and campaigns. We all have a role in stopping the erosion of our democracy," Moss said about the controversy over the audio clip.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker and Moss for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Trump scores Supreme Court win on mail-in voting restrictions before midterms
item.description: The Supreme Court’s order clears the Trump administration to immediately enforce revised mail-ballot restrictions in 23 states ahead of November’s midterms.
item.content:encoded:
In a 6-3 decision, the Supreme Court handed the Trump administration a victory on Monday, allowing it to enforce President Donald Trump’s "election integrity" executive order restricting mail-in voting ahead of the November midterms.

The high court lifted an injunction that had blocked the order in 23 states that challenged it after the administration appealed in July.

The U.S. Postal Service and Justice Department said they would immediately implement the revised mail-ballot restrictions after the ruling.

Most immediately, the ruling clears the path for the U.S. Postal Service to check its distribution of mail-in ballots against a list of citizens maintained by the Department of Homeland Security. But it’s also a significant political victory for the Trump administration as it has advocated against the widespread use of mail-in-voting, citing what it believes is a heightened vulnerability to tampering and voter fraud.

USPS PUBLISHES RULE TO BLOCK MAIL-IN BALLOTS FROM STATES THAT DON’T PROVIDE VOTER LISTS

Most recently, Trump slammed what he called a suspiciously high volume of mail-in-ballots cast for Cynthia Raman in the 2026 LA mayoral race primaries.

"You know, they don’t have voting booths; everything’s by mail. I don’t think a Republican can win in California unless you pass the Save America Act," Trump told Fox News, referring to GOP legislation to narrow the scope of mail-in voting and voter-ID requirements.

"They’re going to have to get rid of mail-in voting."

Like many onlooking conservatives, Trump pointed out that, after election night, the vast majority of Democratic votes had been for Nithya Raman, creating a delayed outpouring of support.

Fox News Digital has not reviewed any particular case of election fraud tied to the LA mayoral race.

SPENCER PRATT LOSES GROUND TO DEMOCRAT WHILE HILTON MAINTAINS LEAD IN LATEST CALIFORNIA BALLOT BATCH DROP

Even so, Trump’s original executive order looked to eliminate any ambiguity. Titled "Preserving and protecting the integrity of American elections," it directed federal agencies to compile citizenship-based lists of eligible voters and ordered the U.S. Postal Service to deliver mail-in ballots only to people appearing on those approved lists.

"Several Federal laws, including 18 U.S.C. 1015 and 611, prohibit foreign nationals from registering to vote or voting in Federal elections.  Yet States fail adequately to vet voters’ citizenship, and, in recent years, the Department of Justice has failed to prioritize and devote sufficient resources for enforcement of these provisions," the executive order reads.

Where critics of the order saw a federal effort to dictate the terms of state-run elections, the court on Monday sided with the administration, stating that the way the executive order was made put requirements only on federal agencies.

In essence, the order didn’t put any new requirements on the states themselves.

"[It] directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to take appropriate action to create and distribute State Citizenship Lists. This provision is an internal directive from the President to a subordinate. It imposes no obligations on the States, so they ‘suffer no concrete harm from’ it, and without concrete harm, there is no standing," the court wrote.

Justices Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented.

CALIFORNIA ELECTION LIMBO FUELED BY 4 PRESSURE POINTS DRAGGING OUT VOTE COUNT, EXPERT SAYS

Notably, the court stipulated that the ruling narrowly addresses the injunction that had prevented its implementation and does not speak to the lawfulness of the order itself. Further legal challenges against the order may still come down the road.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: WNBA reportedly says Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are ineligible, but won't explain why
item.description: The WNBA reportedly declared Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White ineligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft but has not defined "woman" under its CBA.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA has apparently decided Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White aren't eligible to play in the league.

Now it needs to say, on the record, how it reached that decision.

WNBA SILENT AFTER CAITLIN CLARK SAYS LEAGUES SHOULD DETERMINE WHO SHOULD BE INCLUDED IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

Front Office Sports reported Monday that unnamed league sources said Freedom and White, two former NBA players who have declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft, are ineligible.

The sources also called their declarations "simply publicity stunts" and said the league would not give oxygen to efforts intended to mock it or demean others.

Fine.

What makes them ineligible?

That's the only question that matters, and the WNBA still won't answer it.

Freedom and White are obviously making a point. Nobody thinks either man is seriously preparing to spend next season trying to earn a WNBA roster spot.

But calling it a stunt doesn't make the point go away.

The WNBA's collective bargaining agreement says only players who are women are eligible to play in the league. As the FOS report itself acknowledges, the CBA does not define "woman" or include language about "gender identity" or "sex assigned at birth."

That's a problem for the WNBA, and it's not a problem that was created by Freedom or White.

CLUELESS WNBA ATTACKS 'BAD-FAITH' FANS WHO DON'T WANT BIOLOGICAL MEN RUINING WOMEN'S SPORTS

If the league has now determined that two males who say they identify as women do not satisfy the eligibility standard, it should be able to explain the standard it used.

Does the WNBA define "woman" based on biological sex? If so, say it.

Is self-identification insufficient? If so, say that too.

Does the league use a different set of criteria for someone who identifies as transgender? If it does, players and prospective draft entrants deserve to know those criteria before the 2027 WNBA Draft.

The league has reportedly already made the call. It says neither Freedom nor White can play.

Now it needs to explain its rule.

The WNBA doesn't get to make that determination anonymously, dismiss the challenge as a publicity stunt and pretend there is nothing to discuss.

OutKick asked the WNBA to confirm whether the FOS report reflects its official position, identify the criteria used to determine Freedom and White are ineligible, define "woman" under Article XIII, Section 1(a) of the CBA and say whether the league will publish written guidance before the draft.

The WNBA didn't respond to our request before publication.

It did, however, have unnamed sources tell Front Office Sports that Freedom and White are ineligible.

Nobody can prove the WNBA chose Front Office Sports because it expected an easy story. But Salao's coverage gives the league every reason to believe it would get one.

WNBA FIGHT OVER MALES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS EXPOSES HOW THE LEFT KEEPS ANSWERING A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED

Earlier this month, FOS described OutKick as an outlet that had "glommed onto" the issue and ran a subhead about outlets that "pop in to write about transgender issues." The reporter didn't write that as a simple credential story. He adopted the league's premise that OutKick was trying to manufacture a controversy.

FOS also used the Sky's credential decision to make OutKick look unreliable.

It reported that, "as of Friday morning," a Sky source said no decision had been made, then emphasized that OutKick had not shared a rejection email. The Sky denied the request at approximately 3:45 p.m. ET. FOS published at 5:46 p.m. and updated at 8:07 p.m. without telling readers that the denial had already happened.

Maybe that was all a coincidence. It would mean the Sky source had no idea Friday morning how the request would be resolved, nobody told FOS when it was denied and no one at FOS thought to check before it published or updated.

That's a lot to believe.

When OutKick reported something inconvenient for the league, FOS wanted documentation, competing sources and context about OutKick's motives.

But FOS's own report says the CBA does not define the central term, then prints an anonymous claim that Freedom and White are ineligible without explaining how the WNBA reached that conclusion.

The story gives readers no indication the reporter asked the league to define "woman," identify the eligibility criteria it applied to Freedom and White or explain whether self-identification would ever be sufficient. And if he did ask those questions, the story should have told readers that the WNBA wouldn't answer them.

It did neither.

Instead, readers got the WNBA's conclusion and its "publicity stunt" label, not the reporting needed to support either one.

For weeks, the WNBA said there were no immediate eligibility matters to address. Then unnamed league sources told Front Office Sports that Freedom and White are ineligible.

That is an eligibility determination.

The league reportedly made it. It now needs to explain the rule behind it.

item.title: Trump administration touts ‘hard reset’ for American schools, vows to put parents ‘back in charge’
item.description: The president, who was joined by Education Secretary Linda McMahon, said his education agenda will expand school choice, boost support for families and give parents a greater say in their children’s education.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Monday marked the back-to-school season by promoting his administration’s school choice agenda and pledging to put parents "back in charge" of where and how their children are educated.

Speaking at a White House event alongside Education Secretary Linda McMahon, students, parents and educators, Trump said his administration is working to expand school choice while removing what he called "far left extremism" from classrooms.

"We're putting the parents back in charge," Trump said. "They're the ones that love our children. They're the ones that should be in charge."

Trump argued that despite how much the U.S. spends on education, student outcomes should be stronger and families need more schooling options.

NEW YORK JOINS FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE INITIATIVE DESPITE TRADITIONAL DEMOCRAT OPPOSITION

"We want every parent to have the power to send their child to a high-quality school that shares their values. It's so important," Trump said.

The president highlighted the Education Freedom Tax Credit, which beginning in 2027, will offer taxpayers a credit of up to $1,700 for eligible donations to scholarship-granting organizations.

Those organizations can provide scholarships for education-related expenses, including private school tuition, tutoring, school fees and classroom supplies. The funds can also benefit students attending public schools.

The White House said nearly 52 million students could be eligible for the Education Freedom Tax Credit.

DEMOCRATS AIM TO KILL SCHOOL CHOICE FROM WISCONSIN TO THE REST OF THE US

Trump also highlighted changes to 529 education savings plans that allow families to withdraw up to $20,000 annually for K-12 expenses, doubling the previous limit.

Several parents joined Trump at the event to describe how expanded school choice could help their families.

Caleb Griffith, a North Carolina father of five who said his family includes two children with special needs, said the Education Freedom Tax Credit will give his children "access to the services they need to be successful in the most formative years of their lives."

"I want to tell you, we only get one chance to educate our children, and our children are the future of America," Griffith said.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TARGETS HEAD START BUREAUCRACY IN MOVE ADVOCATES SAY PUTS PARENTS IN THE DRIVER'S SEAT

McMahon said the administration is seeking what she described as a "hard reset" in American education, with a goal of returning "to common sense."

"This school year, American parents and students have so much to be excited about because the Trump administration is steering education back to its rightful focus, serving students so that they are prepared for successful futures," McMahon said.

item.title: Mariska Hargitay nearly left 'Law & Order SVU' over fear of being a 'one-trick pony'
item.description: Mariska Hargitay revealed she once told Julianna Margulies she needed to leave "SVU," but her blunt response changed everything.
item.content:encoded:
Mariska Hargitay once considered leaving "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit" after more than two decades as Olivia Benson because she worried the role had come to define her career.

In a new interview with Variety, the actress — who has starred as Benson since "SVU" premiered in 1999 — said she began questioning her future on the long-running NBC drama around its 25th season.

"I’ve got to leave the show too. I don’t want people to think I’m a one-trick pony," Hargitay recalled telling "ER" co-star Julianna Margulies.

'THE BIG BANG THEORY' STAR JIM PARSONS SAYS HE PAID A STEEP PRICE FOR FAME

Margulies, who famously left "ER" after six seasons, had a blunt response.

"Sweetheart, that ship’s sailed," Hargitay said Margulies told her.

While Benson made her a household name, the Emmy winner admitted she often felt constrained creatively due to the grueling production schedule.

"The comedy thing was painful to me because I felt like I was only exercising one part of myself," Hargitay said. "People would say, ‘You need to get off that show and do comedy. You need to get off that show and have a talk show.’"

‘X-FILES’ STAR GILLIAN ANDERSON REVEALS PARENTING REGRET, SAYS SHE WISHES SHE WAS 'LESS SELFISH'

"I wasn’t ready to leave, because I loved it," she said. "And then I got to do all this other stuff, and that’s why I don’t think about leaving right now. Do I want to quit now? No. Why? I made a movie while shooting; I did a play for six weeks on hiatus. I’m hosting the Emmys."

In 2023, Hargitay opened up to Fox News Digital about franchise creator and producer Dick Wolf's "great writing." 

"Dick Wolf is truly a visionary," she said Tuesday. "And I think that's a very singular thing to be a true visionary who understands our culture in a very deep way, but also understands it's sort of ironic that a crime show would be actually calming in a way to our nervous system, knowing that somebody is out there taking care of it."

She continued, "That our voices are heard and there are people that are on it. So that is it."

MARISKA HARGITAY JOKES ABOUT BEING LONGTIME ‘LAW & ORDER’ CO-STAR CHRIS MELONI'S ‘SECOND WIFE’

"It's a very sort of interesting dichotomy," Hargitay added. "Because you think about a crime show, which normally should sort of upset your nervous system, actually can settle it down because of that."

"Law & Order's" success spawned seven spinoffs, including "Special Victims Unit," "Criminal Intent," "Trial by Jury," "LA," "UK," "True Crime" and "Organized Crime."

KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS SURPRISING REASON 'FRASIER' ALMOST NEVER HAPPENED

In 2019, "SVU" became the longest-running live-action television series in history. Hargitay has starred as Detective Olivia Benson in the police procedural since its premiere in 1999 and became an executive producer in 2016.

Fox News Digital's Larry Fink contributed to this post.
